title: Tor base change along a flat coefficient extension
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, let R\to A\to B be homomorphisms of commutative rings, and assume that B is flat as an A-module. For every R-module M and every n\ge 0, the canonical coefficient-base-change map $$\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_{n}(M,A)\otimes_A B\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_{n}(M,B)$$ is an isomorphism. Consequently, if A\to B is faithfully flat and $\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_{n}(M,B)=0$, then $\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_{n}(M,A)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Lemma Tag 00M8 (algebra-lemma-flat-base-change-tor), whose free-resolution proof applies verbatim with a fixed base ring R and flat coefficient extension A -> B.

proof.text: Choose a free $R$-resolution $P\to M$ by applying [lem-weil-pbc-free-resolution-ses-split] to $0\to M\xrightarrow{1}M\to0\to0$. Put $C=P\otimes_R A$, $D=P\otimes_R B$, omitting augmentations and extending $P$ by zero below degree zero. By [lem-trf-tor-resolution-coefficient-actions], the canonical maps $\iota_A:\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A)\cong H_n(C)$ and $\iota_B:\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,B)\cong H_n(D)$ respect the coefficient actions and their scalar tower.

Use [lem-trf-tor-coefficient-resolution-map] to obtain the coefficient chain map $\phi:C\to\operatorname{Res}_gD$ and its $B$-linear homology extension $\alpha_n$. Apply [lem-pc-flat-scalar-extension-homology-adjunct] with its rings $(A,E,D)$ replaced by $(R,A,B)$ and its complex $Q^j=P_{-j}$ with differential $d_P$. The lemma's coefficient-left formula $a\otimes p\mapsto g(a)\otimes p$ is exactly $\phi$ after the tensor switches $p\otimes a\leftrightarrow a\otimes p$. Its hypotheses require only the assumed flatness of $A\to B$. Degree $-n$ gives that $\alpha_n$ is invertible, including $n=0$. The commuting square in [lem-trf-tor-coefficient-resolution-map] gives $c_n=\iota_B^{-1}\alpha_n(\iota_A\otimes1_B)$. All three factors are $B$-linear isomorphisms; hence the specified canonical map is an isomorphism.

Now assume $A\to B$ is faithfully flat and $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,B)=0$. Put $T=\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A)$. The proved isomorphism gives $T\otimes_A B=0$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives the switch isomorphism $B\otimes_A T\cong T\otimes_A B$, $b\otimes t\mapsto t\otimes b$, whose inverse is the same switch. Thus tensoring the complex $0\to T\to0$ on the left with $B$ produces an exact zero complex. By the reflection of exactness in [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], $0\to T\to0$ is exact at $T$. Its kernel there is $T$ and its image is $0$, so $T=0$, as required.
